transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess what brings me in is that I've been feeling... well, maybe just a little overly energetic lately? 

I mean, I teach special ed, so being active is a good thing, but I feel like I'm constantly running on a motor. Like, I'll finish one thing at school, or even at home, and I just immediately jump right into the next project. It's just getting to where I can never really shut myself off. I'm sure it's probably not a huge deal, maybe I'm just keeping myself a bit too busy, but... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you usually help people with?
During this time, have you found that you need less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I definitely still need my sleep. I mean, if I don't get a full night, I certainly feel it the next day. Teaching takes a lot out of you, as you can probably imagine! 

So, no, I definitely don't feel rested if I try to get by on less sleep than usual. I still need my regular hours. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers for what you're looking for.
Do you find yourself frequently worrying about a lot of different everyday things?

Um, well... no, I don't think I do. I mean, I have the normal concerns anyone has—making sure my students are doing okay, keeping up with things around the house—but I wouldn't call myself a worrier. 

I actually try to be a pretty upbeat person. Since I'm always kind of moving from one project to the next, I don't really stop to dwell on things too much. I hope it's okay that I don't have that issue? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you an accurate picture of what's going on.
Have there ever been periods in your life where you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, sure, everyone has a bad day here or there, especially when the kids are having a tough week, but... no, I've never had a time where I felt really down or stopped caring about things. 

I'm usually pretty positive, actually! I love my job, I love staying busy... I just try to keep a smile on my face and keep moving forward. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want to make it sound like I'm depressed when I'm really just... well, a bit too energized, you know? Is it helpful that I don't feel that way?
Has this feeling of being constantly on the go or driven by a motor been present since you were a child?

Oh, yes, definitely. Um, it's always been this way, really. My mother... well, she actually used to joke that even back in elementary school, I basically taught the class from my seat. I was just, you know, always popping out of my chair, or talking, or... maybe cutting in a little before the teacher had even finished giving directions. I was just a very eager kid, I suppose! 

So, yes, this has just been a part of who I am long before adulthood. It's certainly not something that just started recently with the family changes we've had. I hope it's okay to share that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right history so you have the full picture. Does that help answer your question?
